items.abstract: <jats:p>Lee, Vindas-Meléndez, and Wang conjectured a disk bound for the roots of Ehrhart polynomials of generalized-snake order polytopes. The printed statement has a sign error and an off-by-one length parameter; we use the unique repair compatible with their definition and their proved functional equation. We give exact computer-assisted counterexamples for the regular snake words of lengths 9 and 10. For length 10, the requested next finite layer, the word εLRLRLRLRLR has a root ρ satisfying |ρ + 7| &gt; 6. A rational Rouché disk proves the strict inequality without floating-point roots. A separate verifier reconstructs the Ehrhart polynomial from order-ideal multichains and certifies the same failure through an exact Cayley transform and Routh table. The length-9 example also shows that the authors' reported computation through length 9 is incompatible with the corrected statement.</jats:p>
title: Exact Counterexamples to an Ehrhart Root-Disk Conjecture for Generalized Snake Posets

items.abstract: <jats:p>A conjecture of Sokal [24], regarding the domain of nonvanishing for independence polynomials of graphs, states that given any natural number Δ≥3, there exists a neighborhood in C of the interval [0,(Δ−1)Δ−1/(Δ−2)Δ) on which the independence polynomial of any graph with maximum degree at most Δ does not vanish. We show here that Sokal’s conjecture holds, as well as a multivariate version, and prove the optimality for the domain of nonvanishing. An important step is to translate the setting to the language of complex dynamical systems.</jats:p>
title: On a Conjecture of Sokal Concerning Roots of the Independence Polynomial
